title: Microsoft Stock (MSFT) Falls 2.2% on Claude Sheets Launch (Nov 10)
summary: Microsoft (MSFT) fell 2.20% to $533.16 on Nov 10 as financial media tied the drop to Anthropic's Claude Sheets launch, an Excel competitor.
body_markdown:
## Why Microsoft Stock Fell


The main reported cause was new competition for Excel, Microsoft's spreadsheet software. According to[Anthropic's announcement](https://claude.com/resources/articles/more-ways-to-work-with-claude-sheets-whiteboards-and-interactive-connectors) on November 10, Claude Sheets lets teams and Claude "build spreadsheets together, collaboratively organize data, create and edit formulas, and work across multiple tabs." As reported by[Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2312177/anthropic-takes-on-google-and-microsoft-with-claude-sheets/) , files built in Claude Sheets can be exported to Excel, and the tool is in beta for Claude subscribers on web, desktop and mobile.


[Barron's](https://finance.yahoo.com/m/57e7d2d0-e7dd-3ca4-ab38-8cdf91a80697/microsoft-stock-falls-as.html) linked Microsoft's decline to the launch, describing Claude Sheets as an Excel competitor that lets customers build full spreadsheets from simple prompts. The publication also noted that Microsoft has ways to defend itself against the competition.


The session also reshuffled the market-value rankings. Per[Benzinga](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/microsoft-briefly-overtakes-nvidia-jensen-230016006.html) , Microsoft briefly overtook Nvidia on Tuesday to become the world's second-most valuable company for the first time since June 2025, as fallout from[Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-spy-affair-scrutiny-trump-fbi-probe-china-chips-nvda-shares/) deepened Nvidia's selloff and erased the $1.84 trillion market-value lead Nvidia held on October 6. Benzinga noted that Nvidia regained second place by early afternoon.


## MSFT Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Cloud growth:[Microsoft's fiscal first-quarter results](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/fy-2027-q1/press-release-webcast) , released October 28, showed revenue up 19% to $92.3 billion and Azure revenue up 48%.
- Contracted demand: the same[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) showed commercial remaining performance obligation up 73% to $677 billion and Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9 billion, up 30%.
- In-house chips: Benzinga reported that Microsoft is developing its own Maia chips, which already handle some Copilot workloads, with plans to deploy them at a much larger scale starting in 2027.


### Risks


- New competition: Claude Sheets moves Anthropic into spreadsheet work, a launch Engadget framed as Anthropic taking on Google and Microsoft.
- Heavy AI spending: Benzinga reported that Microsoft spent $45.2 billion on infrastructure last quarter, much of it benefiting Nvidia, whose chips power its AI services.
- Relative weakness: Microsoft fell 1.46 percentage points more than the Nasdaq Composite, on volume 11.20% above average.


Benzinga added that Nvidia reports earnings on November 17, leaving the race for second place among the most valuable companies unsettled.
